newsitem.title: USA: "Jedi" returns in style, tops U.S. box office sales.
newsitem.headline: "Jedi" returns in style, tops U.S. box office sales.

text.p: "Return of the Jedi," the third installment in the "Star Wars" trilogy, completed a clean sweep for the series' reissue by taking top spot at the box office over the weekend, according to estimates Sunday.

"Jedi," originally released in 1983, took in an estimated $16.3 million in ticket sales over the Friday to Sunday weekend, according to Exhibitor Relations Co., which tracks sales for the studios. The movie has sold $280 million worth of tickets in the United States including its first release.

It came in comfortably ahead of the Tim Allen comedy "Jungle 2 Jungle," which held second place with $11.3 million in ticket sales. Last week's number one, "Private Parts," tumbled to third with sales of about $9 million.
Meanwhile, the reissued "Star Wars," came in ninth with $2.3 million in sales while "The Empire Strikes Back" shared fourth spot with $5.5 million in sales.

Comparisons with how "Jedi" did in its first time release are difficult since it opened on a Wednesday before a Memorial Day holiday weekend. Back then, it earned $6.2 million on its first day and $41.1 million after its first six days.

The reissued version, like the other two, features a cleaned-up soundtrack and visuals. Several scenes have also been expanded. The movie, released by News Corp.'s 20th Century Fox, averaged $7,721 from 2,111 screens.

By contrast, the reissued "Star Wars" opened with $35.9 million for a $17,066 average during the Jan. 31-Feb. 2 weekend while "The Empire Strikes Back" opened with $22 million and a $10,410 average during the Feb. 21-23 weekend.
The lifetime total for "Star Wars" is $456.7 million and for "The Empire Strikes Back" is $282 million.
The top 10 contained one other new entry, the urban romance "Love Jones," which opened in sixth place with $4 million in sales. It is released by New Line Cinema, a unit of Time Warner Inc.

The Academy Award-nominated "Sling Blade" jumped nine places to seventh with $3 million as its number of screens jumped to 951 from 268. The quirky drama, which has won Oscar nominations for screenplay and acting for Billy Bob Thornton, is released by Miramax Films, a unit of Walt Disney Co.
"Private Parts" suffered a hefty 38 percent decline in sales, the biggest among top earners. The blunt radio host Howard Stern's film was released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.
"The Empire Strikes back" shared fourth with the mob picture "Donnie Brasco," the TriStar Pictures release whose receipts fell 30 percent in its third weekend. TriStar is owned by Sony Corp.
